sourceCopy.name: Color Mixer
sourceCopy.title: Color Mixer — Free HEX & RGB Tool | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Mix two or more colors by weight. Compare sRGB and linear-light results, build a color ramp, and copy HEX, RGB, or HSL values free.
sourceCopy.intro: Blend colors with editable weights, compare two digital mixing modes, and build a swatch ramp between the first two colors. Nothing is uploaded.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How do I mix two colors online?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Choose two or more colors, set each weight, and select sRGB or linear-light mixing. The result shows HEX, RGB, and HSL values.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. Color calculations run locally in your browser. No account or image upload is needed.

fields.accuracyNote: The selected method affects the result. sRGB blends displayed channel values; linear light converts channels before mixing.
fields.pigmentNote: This predicts digital screen colors, not how real paint or pigments will mix.
fields.privacyNote: Runs in this browser. Colors are not uploaded or automatically saved.

additionalFaqs.question: Why do sRGB and linear-light mixes look different?
additionalFaqs.answer: sRGB averages the encoded screen channel values. Linear-light mode converts them to light values first, mixes, then converts back. The chosen method changes the result.

additionalFaqs.question: Can this predict the color of mixed paint?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. This is digital color math for screens, not a physical pigment model. Real paint depends on pigment properties, transparency, concentration, lighting, and the surface.

additionalFaqs.question: What color formats can I copy?
additionalFaqs.answer: The result displays HEX, RGB, and HSL. You can copy the HEX value or download a small CSS color palette.
